snippets.output: A 27-year-old man with fatigue, cough, and 15-pound weight loss over 3 weeks has been diagnosed with tuberculosis based on a positive QuantiFERON gold test.

The standard initial treatment for active tuberculosis in a 27-year-old man with fatigue, cough, 15-pound weight loss over 3 weeks, recent release from prison, intravenous drug use in prison, and a positive QuantiFERON gold test includes isoniazid, rifampin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol.

Elevated liver enzymes can be a serious side effect of tuberculosis treatment in a 27-year-old man with fatigue, cough, 15-pound weight loss over 3 weeks, recent release from prison, intravenous drug use in prison, a positive QuantiFERON gold test, and started on treatment for tuberculosis, but elevated liver enzymes do not typically necessitate the immediate discontinuation of all tuberculosis medications.
Elevated liver enzymes in a 27-year-old man started on treatment for tuberculosis might require dose adjustment or closer monitoring.

Hyperuricemia alone usually does not require discontinuation of tuberculosis treatment in a 27-year-old man with fatigue, cough, 15-pound weight loss over 3 weeks, recent release from prison, intravenous drug use in prison, a positive QuantiFERON gold test, and initiation of tuberculosis therapy.

Hyperuricemia during tuberculosis treatment in a 27-year-old man recently released from prison with fatigue, cough, 15-pound weight loss over 3 weeks, intravenous drug use in prison, and a positive QuantiFERON gold test might require discontinuation of treatment if it leads to symptomatic gout.
Ethambutol can cause optic neuritis, which can lead to vision loss.
Optic neuritis warrants discontinuation of ethambutol in a 27-year-old man started on treatment for tuberculosis to prevent permanent damage.
Isoniazid can cause peripheral neuropathy, and peripheral neuropathy can often be managed with pyridoxine (vitamin B6) supplementation.

In a 27-year-old man recently released from prison with fatigue, cough, 15-pound weight loss over 3 weeks, a positive QuantiFERON gold test, and started on tuberculosis treatment, optic neuritis is the most likely indication to discontinue treatment, whereas peripheral neuropathy does not necessarily require discontinuing treatment.
Rifampin can cause red-orange discoloration of body fluids such as urine, sweat, and tears, and these red body excretions are a benign side effect.
Red body excretions do not require discontinuation of tuberculosis treatment in a 27-year-old man with a positive QuantiFERON gold test who was started on treatment for tuberculosis.

Optic neuritis is the most severe side effect for a 27-year-old man with fatigue, cough, 15-pound weight loss over 3 weeks, recent release from prison, intravenous drug use in prison, a positive QuantiFERON gold test, and started on treatment for tuberculosis.
Optic neuritis warrants immediate discontinuation of the offending drug, ethambutol, in a 27-year-old man started on treatment for tuberculosis, to prevent permanent vision loss.
